You will explore topics such as media relations, crisis communication, social media strategy, advertising campaigns, and intercultural communication. With a focus on ethical and socially responsible communication, our program emphasizes the importance of diversity, inclusion, and global perspectives in today’s interconnected world.
Program name: Strategic Communication, Public Relations & Advertising - BA

description: Sacred Heart’s Theatre Arts BA program challenges students to hone their skills as performers, designers, technicians, stage managers, directors, producers, and educators. This program provides students with a strong foundation in all areas of theatre through coursework that emphasizes collaboration, creativity, critical thinking, and communication skills. A Theatre Arts major will develop a comprehensive understanding of dramatic literature, theatre history, and contemporary theatre practices. Students also learn how to create and produce theatrical performances, from concept to curtain. Our faculty are experts in their fields, bringing a wealth of professional experience to the classroom. They are dedicated to helping students achieve their artistic and academic goals.

A Theatre Arts minor helps students enhance their acting, directing, design, and technical skills while providing a deeper understanding of the history and theory of theatre. Students are immersed in creating, experiencing, and studying theatre both inside and outside the classroom. They have the opportunity to participate in main stage productions through the Department of Theatre Arts Program, student-run productions through TheatreFest, and various workshops. Theatre arts minors develop valuable skills in critical thinking, public speaking, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

The undergraduate major in Theology and Religious Studies introduces students to the academic study of religion as a human phenomenon. It seeks to understand religion's diverse expressions (beliefs, texts, ethics, rituals, institutions, communities, and experiences) in various historical and cultural contexts, paying particular attention to the Christian tradition and its Catholic expression. Students gain an understanding of religion's influence on societies and individuals globally and domestically, along with an appreciation for religious diversity in the world today. The program aims to develop religiously literate citizens of the world, capable of critical inquiry and constructive engagement with religious traditions and issues related to religion and society. A student majoring in Theology and Religious Studies will engage in historical, textual, theological, and ethical inquiry, and learn to apply theoretical and methodological tools for understanding religion. The Theology and Religious Studies program offers an excellent foundation for graduate studies and professions in education, law, social work, journalism, public service, and ministry.

A minor in Theology and Religious Studies provides students with the opportunity to explore profound questions concerning religious traditions, practices, and beliefs. Theology and Religious Studies minors foster critical thinking, ethical reasoning, and cultural understanding, preparing students to engage with diverse perspectives and make informed decisions in an increasingly complex world. Students with a minor in Theology and Religious Studies are well-equipped to contribute to professions that require cultural competence and ethical deliberation, such as education, social work, law, healthcare, journalism, and ministry.

The Web Design & Development minor at Sacred Heart University is designed for students interested in learning the fundamental principles and techniques of creating and maintaining dynamic websites. This minor provides a blend of design aesthetics, user experience (UX) principles, and technical development skills, preparing students to build engaging and functional web solutions. Students will explore front-end development (HTML, CSS, JavaScript), back-end basics, content management systems (CMS), and responsive design, equipping them with a comprehensive skill set for the digital age. This minor is suitable for students from various disciplines who wish to enhance their digital literacy and career prospects in web-related fields.

The Women, Gender and Sexuality Studies minor provides an interdisciplinary lens through which students can analyze gendered power relations in society, politics, and culture. The minor examines gender as a social construct, intersecting with race, class, sexuality, ability, and religion to shape human experience. Students will develop critical thinking skills necessary to analyze historical and contemporary understandings of gender and sexuality and their impact on individuals and communities. Students will be exposed to feminist theory, gender theory, and queer theory, and will learn how these frameworks are used to analyze various topics such as masculinity, globalization, human rights, and social justice. The WGSS minor will provide students with marketable skills that complement majors across the university. The minor will prepare students for a range of careers in fields such as social work, public policy, non-profit organizations, education, journalism, and advocacy, among others. Students will be encouraged to explore opportunities for community engagement and internships in gender and sexuality-related organizations.
